requirement: Raise informative exceptions for failed calls to a JSON API, reading the machine code and message from its error envelope and falling back gracefully when the body is not the expected JSON.
skeleton: A message length constant, an ApiError with status, code and message, a NotFoundError subclass, and raise_for_api_error skipping ok responses, decoding JSON defensively, reading the error envelope or truncated text, and choosing the exception class by status.
caption: Converting failed requests responses from a JSON API into typed exceptions. ApiError is an Exception carrying status, code and message; NotFoundError subclasses it. raise_for_api_error(resp) returns quietly when resp.ok, so 2xx and 3xx never raise. Otherwise it tries resp.json and treats requests.JSONDecodeError as no body. If the body is a dict whose error value is itself a dict, code comes from it defaulting to unknown and message defaulting to empty; any other shape, such as HTML or a string error, uses code unknown and the response text cut to MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS, 200. A 404 raises NotFoundError and every other failure raises ApiError. The fixture asserts, with hand built responses, that 200, 201 and 304 pass, that a 422 envelope yields an exact ApiError with its code and message, that a 404 raises NotFoundError, that an HTML 502 gives unknown with the first 200 characters, and that a string error or missing message falls back safely.

plan.intent: Give callers actionable API failures instead of bare HTTPError
constraints: Invalid JSON bodies are handled via requests.JSONDecodeError
The envelope is used only when error is a dict
Fallback messages are the text cut to 200 characters

rationale.teaches: Check resp.ok, decode error bodies defensively, validate the envelope shape before indexing, and map statuses to exception subclasses.
rationale.why: Proxies return HTML error pages, some servers send a string error, and assuming the envelope turns an API failure into a JSONDecodeError or AttributeError.

ops.docstring: Turn HTTP error responses from a JSON API into typed exceptions.

ops.source:
class ApiError(Exception):
    """An error response with its status, machine code and message."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"{status} {code}: {message}")
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message

class NotFoundError(ApiError):
    """The requested resource does not exist."""

candidates.why_wrong: A 201 or 304 response is treated as an API error.
An HTML error page raises JSONDecodeError instead of ApiError.
Fallback messages are cut to 100 characters instead of 200.
A 404 raises plain ApiError instead of NotFoundError.
A string error value crashes with AttributeError instead of falling back.
